American English — contextual meaning: isolation — separating people to limit contact; in the story, sick people are kept apart from the group.
alphabet — the ordered set of letters used by a language.
bacteriologist — a specialist who studies bacteria. Granser uses the term when recalling the researchers of his former world.
barge — a broad boat used to carry people, animals or cargo.
shell; carapace — the hard covering that protects an animal such as a crab.
chauffeur; driver — someone whose job is driving vehicles. This was Bill's work before the plague; Chauffeur becomes his name.
contagion; transmission of infection — the passing of an infectious disease. The refugees fear that someone may already be infected.
convulsion — a strong, involuntary muscular movement. Narrative form: «convulsiones».
skull — the bony structure of the head. The boys find skulls among the human remains.
to decompose — here used as «descomponerse», to decay or rot; the bodies begin to decay soon after death.
airship — a balloon-like aircraft that can be steered.
illness; disease — a condition that affects health. The Scarlet Plague is the fictional disease in this story.
epidemic — the spread of a disease affecting many people in a region during a particular period.
scarlet — a vivid, intense red. It names the color associated with the fictional plague.
forge — a hearth or workshop where metal is heated so that it can be shaped.
germ — a microorganism, especially one that can cause disease. Narrative form: «gérmenes».
campfire; bonfire — a fire built outdoors. The boys eat beside one on the beach.
sling — a flexible strap used to throw stones.
footprint; track — a mark left by a person or animal passing through. Granser follows tracks to find other survivors.
fire; conflagration — a destructive fire spreading through a place. Fires consume the cities during the disaster.
incubation period — the time between infection and the appearance of the first symptoms. In this fictional outbreak, symptoms can be delayed.
immune — protected against a particular disease despite exposure. Granser does not become sick with the plague.
tycoon — a person with great power and influence, especially through wealth. In this story the magnates also hold political power.
pack; herd — a group of animals of the same species. Use pack for dogs or wolves and herd for horses in these contexts.
thicket; scrub — land covered with dense shrubs and other low plants.
mussel — an edible marine animal with two dark shells. The boys cook mussels on the beach.
message — information communicated from one person to another. News of the plague arrives through messages.
microorganism — a living thing generally too small to see without instruments. Not all microorganisms cause disease.
microscope — an instrument for seeing things too small to distinguish with the naked eye.
moccasin — a soft leather shoe without a raised heel. Bill uses an order about his moccasins to humiliate Vesta.
coin — a piece of money, usually metal. Edwin's coin preserves a date that Granser can read.
rust — the coating produced as iron oxidizes. The old rails are rust-covered.
palace; grand residence — a large, luxurious building. Vesta takes refuge on a wealthy family's property.
gunpowder — a substance that burns very rapidly and has been used to propel projectiles.
well — a deep hole dug in the ground to reach or draw water.
provisions; supply — food or other supplies stored for later use. The narrative usually uses the plural «provisiones».
ration — a measured share of food assigned to a person or family.
rail — a metal track on a railroad. Trees have displaced the old rails. The story uses the singular «raíl»; its plural is «raíles».
shelter; refuge — a place where a person or group seeks protection. The Chemistry Building serves as a refuge.
wealth — an abundance of property and economic resources. Wealth does not keep the plague out of the palace.
looter — someone who steals goods, often taking advantage of disorder.
stallion — a male animal kept for breeding; here, an adult male horse leading the herd.
symptom — a sign or manifestation of an illness.
loneliness; solitude — being without company, or the feeling that results. Granser suffers from it despite having food and shelter.
to subjugate; force into obedience — to make someone submit through power or force. Narrative form: «sometida».
medicinal serum — a liquid medical preparation. A message announces a possible remedy, but its effectiveness is not confirmed.
superstition — belief in unproven powers or explanations. The story contrasts such claims with knowledge that can be tested.
embankment — a raised bank of earth built to support a road or railroad.
worker; laborer — someone who works. Granser calls the old society's workers free even though they own very little.
treatment — measures intended to combat an illness; treatment does not always mean a cure.
tribe — a human community with its own social ties. Different groups of survivors form tribes.
university — an institution of higher education. Granser worked at one as a professor.
sail — a sheet of fabric that catches the wind to propel a boat. Granser makes one from old canvas; this is not the meaning candle.
